activities.anchor: The earliest films did not edit
activities.caption: rebuild the invention of the cut, year by year
activities.name: cutInventionOrder

config.prompt: The syntax arrived in one generation — put the milestones in order:
items: Lumière programmes — single scenes, no edits
Méliès joins tableau to tableau, like theatre
Porter's The Great Train Robbery cuts between locations to tell one story
Griffith systematises the toolkit — the close-up, and parallel editing
Intolerance cuts across four eras at once
config.why: Within twenty years the medium had a grammar nobody had planned — the spectator learned to read ellipsis without instruction: this happened later; this happened elsewhere.

activities.anchor: a scene's meaning is fixed on the set
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the folklore about editors
activities.name: cutAssembleSpot

config.prompt: A note on what editors do contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: The edit suite receives the day's material and arranges it in script order.
So the scene's meaning was locked on the set, before the edit began.
The same take plays as triumph or sin depending on what precedes it.
Performances are re-pitched at the timeline.
Scenes can acquire a subject nobody filmed.
config.correction: Meaning is not locked on the set — final cut is authorship: the neighbours write the performance.
config.why: The Kuleshov effect is the rebuttal — which is exactly why the credit is fought over contractually.

activities.anchor: the reach that begins in the wide completes in the medium
activities.caption: pair each rule with the job it does
activities.name: cutRulesMatch

config.prompt: The invisibility toolkit, rule by rule — pair each with its job:

pairs.right: a look off-frame pays off with what the looker sees, placing the world around them
vary angle and size between shots — prevents the stutter of the accidental jump cut
keeps screen direction constant so the mental map survives
hands, the window — they absorb trims and time-jumps
gives the audience a beat of anticipation

config.why: Done right, the spectator never registers an edit — they register a conversation.

activities.anchor: The Bolshevik film school, film-stock-starved and theory-drunk
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the five methods and the rival model
activities.name: cutMontageCloze

config.text: Eisenstein distinguished five methods, from %%0%% (cut to length) through rhythmic and tonal to overtonal and %%1%% (two images colliding to produce an idea) — and argued against Pudovkin's %%2%% model, shots as bricks, for a dialectical one: thesis and antithesis colliding into a synthesis in the spectator.
config.hint: Montage as thought — the Odessa Steps is the demonstration piece a century on.

activities.anchor: Cutting pace is the film's pulse
activities.caption: the accelerando versus the long take — drag between them
activities.name: cutPaceCompare

config.prompt: Two ways to hold time — drag the divider:

before.label: the accelerando
before.text: Shots shorten as confrontation approaches — the classical tension curve. Cutting controls time: the heist cutting against the gala, The Godfather's baptism intercutting sacrament and murder.

after.label: the long take
after.text: Unbroken time, no escape hatch — Children of Men's car ambush makes the audience share the terror's duration rather than its highlight reel.

config.why: Cutting controls time; the long take surrenders control and banks presence — which is why 'when to cut' has no formula, only judgement.

activities.anchor: the camera genuinely never stopped rolling
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the one-shot film
activities.name: cut1917Predict

config.q: 1917 plays as one continuous shot for its whole runtime. Was the camera genuinely never stopped?
choices: Yes — the entire film is a single unbroken take
No — it is a composite: hidden cuts disguised in whip-pans, dark passages and digital stitches
Yes, except for one visible cut at the midpoint
config.why: Both 1917 and Children of Men's car ambush are composites — the experience of unbroken time is manufactured rather than recorded. The long take is an effect built in the edit, by its absence.

activities.anchor: leaps across space or time on a shared form
activities.caption: call the jump — 2001's single cut
activities.name: cutMatchEstimate

config.prompt: 2001's match cut leaps from a thrown bone to an orbiting weapon. Roughly how many years does that one edit compress?
config.why: Four million years compressed into the medium's most consequential single cut — the first tool becomes the ultimate tool (and its darkest joke).
config.context: The jump cut broke continuity on purpose in Breathless (1960) — New Wave honesty telling the audience 'this is constructed'.

activities.caption: file each task: scripted structure, or found structure
activities.name: cutDocBuckets

config.prompt: Two editors, two relationships to structure — file each task:

items.label: shaping material shot to the script's plan
hundreds of hours of vérité rushes whose story does not exist yet
interviews re-ordered into a conversation that never happened
asking which character arc the material supports — and whether the arc is honest to the people filmed

config.why: Every editor is a documentary editor of their footage first — discovering what the material actually supports before imposing what the script assumed.
